column1: F061|Show the whole keepsake and closer views of visible concerns or details that matter to the proposed arrangement. Date the photographs and describe only what you can observe, such as loose parts or curled edges. Avoid unnecessary handling or attempted repair. Keep irreplaceable originals with you until suitability and current transfer instructions are confirmed.|/memory-art

F062|Yes. Record visible condition and any treatment or handling history you actually know. Distinguish your observations from information supplied by someone else. Clear photographs can support the discussion, but they do not establish a diagnosis or preservation suitability. Do not clean, alter or send an irreplaceable item based on a general reference image.|/memory-art

F063|Photographs are an appropriate starting point for discussing what you would like to preserve and its condition. Include a whole view and relevant details, with a simple item list. They do not guarantee that the material is suitable. Wait for the atelier's guidance and confirmed transfer arrangements before sending sentimental originals.|/memory-art

F064|Give each item a reference and explain its significance in a short, relevant note. Mark which items are essential to consider and which are optional. Match photographs to the list. You can explain meaning without sharing unnecessary personal history. Priority does not establish that an item can be preserved or included in the final design.|/memory-art

F065|No. An arrangement reference shows a visual intention, not a guaranteed preservation outcome. Label illustrative or generated imagery and explain which relationships matter, such as orientation or spacing. The actual materials and their condition need assessment. Do not infer permanent colour, exact shape or suitability from a clear floral-block visualization.|/memory-art

F066|Use the preservation or custom-piece brief to describe the materials, condition and intended idea, with clear photographs. Ask specifically about suitability before making transfer arrangements. The current guidance says to keep sentimental originals until the atelier confirms suitability and provides instructions. A catalogue image cannot answer that question for your particular item.|/memory-art

F067|Wait until suitability and current transfer instructions are confirmed for the actual items. Check the recipient, destination and arrangements rather than relying on a general address or an old message. Keep a condition record and item list for the discussion. This answer does not prescribe packing or transport methods for fragile or irreplaceable materials.|/shipping-delivery

F068|Public use is a separate permission decision from a private design request. State which names, dates, images or story details must remain private and review any proposed public wording and photographs against that choice. Do not assume that personalization on an object authorizes the same information to appear in a website story.|/privacy

F069|Collect the different priorities against the same item photographs and proposed arrangement. Identify shared preferences and unresolved choices, then agree who will communicate the consolidated brief. Do not imply consent from absent participants. Material suitability remains a separate question, even if the family agrees on the desired visual direction.|/memory-art

F070|Keep the confirmed details with the current agreed design and specification, including the item references, arrangement and any approved personalization. Preserve earlier preferences as superseded notes rather than mixing them into the current version. A saved inquiry records the request; it does not itself confirm preservation suitability, the final design or production.|/terms

F071|Provide the exact text in a clearly labelled field, preserving capitalization, punctuation and spacing. Keep pronunciation notes and explanatory context separate. If a specific layout matters, show preferred line breaks in addition to the complete text. Review the actual final proof against the source before approval; do not rely on memory or a paraphrase.|/personal-art

F072|You can ask about the intended script and provide the exact preferred text. Have a fluent reader check spelling and meaning, then review the actual proposed layout. Do not assume that an English transliteration determines one approved spelling or that every script is supported. Feasibility and the final proof need individual confirmation.|/personal-art

F073|State the full intended date in words alongside the preferred visible format. This prevents ambiguous numeric dates from being read in the wrong order. Identify separators, month style and any essential line breaks. Keep the occasion date separate from the requested delivery period; a personalization date does not confirm a production or delivery commitment.|/personal-art

F074|Provide the complete text and a second version showing preferred breaks. Mark which groupings are essential and which can change with the design. Check the final proof after any layout revision, including punctuation and spacing. Preferred line breaks do not establish that the wording will fit or remain legible in every proposed format.|/personal-art

F075|You can describe initials as a preference in the personalization brief. Supply the exact characters, order, capitalization and punctuation, and explain whether they replace a full name. Do not leave the atelier to infer the initials from private recipient details. The design, layout and feasibility still need discussion and a reviewed final proof.|/personal-art

F076|Use one item reference per name and keep shared wording separate. Include the source of each spelling and mark whether it has been checked. Review the list in the same order as the proposed set. Blank fields should say whether no text is requested or a decision is pending. Quantity, feasibility and timing require separate agreement.|/personal-art

F077|No. An occasion date explains the purpose and urgency of a request but does not book production or delivery. State your preferred arrival period and any flexibility, then ask what is feasible. Production and delivery estimates are confirmed individually before an order is accepted. A saved website receipt is not a timing commitment.|/shipping-delivery

F078|Share only the recipient information needed for the current private design or delivery discussion. Keep public attribution and story permission separate. A style reference often does not need a recipient's address, workplace or private photographs. If a public image is later proposed, check both its caption and background for identifying details before permission is given.|/privacy

F079|Review spelling in the actual current proof or proposed layout, comparing it with the exact text source. Check names, dates, punctuation, spacing, script and line breaks. A second competent reader can help, especially for another language. Repeat the check after relevant changes; approval of an earlier version does not verify a later revision.|/personal-art

F080|Describe the shared design direction and the details that would vary between items. A small matrix with item references, exact text and optional differences can help. The request is subject to feasibility, quotation and timing discussion. Do not infer availability, a quantity discount or a delivery promise from an illustrative gift-set image.|/commission

F081|Use the collection navigation to browse collectible design, memory art and personal art. Choose the starting point closest to the purpose of your request, and keep useful page links. If the idea crosses categories, explain that in a custom brief. A collection label helps browsing but does not determine every possible variation or confirm feasibility.|/commission

F082|Try an ordinary word describing the form, use or topic, then inspect the titles and result types. Refine a broad search or simplify an overly specific phrase. Keep the relevant page link for later discussion. Search results identify available website content; they do not confirm stock, suitability, price or an accepted service request.|/search

F083|Use the active filter control or remove chip offered beside the selected choice, or choose Clear filters to begin again. Check the remaining applied choices if the list is still narrow. Filters only change the displayed results. They do not alter saved content, create new entries or establish that a particular piece is suitable for your use.|/journal

F084|Saved pieces are kept in this browser's local storage. They provide a shortlist, not an order, reservation or confirmed quotation. Keep your own reference links and notes for anything important, particularly before changing browsers or clearing site data. Use the saved list to prepare the later conversation rather than treating it as a purchase record.|/saved-pieces

F085|No automatic cross-device sharing is provided by the current saved-pieces feature. It uses the browser's local storage, so another device or browser can have a different list. Keep useful links and your reasons for saving them separately if you need to continue elsewhere. Clearing browser data may also remove the local shortlist.|/saved-pieces

F086|The RLA inquiry reference identifies a saved request. A quotation or proposal revision identifies a particular version of a later document. Keep both with their dates and use the relevant one in follow-up messages. Neither identifier alone proves payment, acceptance or a production booking. Ask for clarification if the current proposal version is unclear.|/contact

F087|Compare the inquiry reference, names, exact personalization text, dimensions, dates, paragraph order and any added notes. Check that the pasted message is complete and directed to the intended conversation. Clipboard content can differ from what you expect. The website prepares a summary, but you review and press Send yourself; it cannot verify that action.|/faq

F088|Read the pasted message in the destination application before sending. Compare section boundaries and the order of details with the saved summary, especially around names, dates and long notes. Restore missing breaks without changing the meaning. Do not assume a correct website preview guarantees identical formatting after the text passes through a clipboard or another application.|/faq

F089|Read the visible error and check whether a successful receipt or RLA reference exists. A failed message handoff after saving is different from a failed save; use the existing receipt's Open WhatsApp or Copy controls in that case. If the outcome is uncertain, avoid repeated submissions and contact the atelier with the information you have.|/contact

F090|Keep catalogue links and inquiry references as identifiers for the discussion, and keep any agreed quotation and payment arrangements in their own current record. The website does not take payment or confirm a production booking. Do not treat a saved piece, receipt or price-related reference as proof that a later payment arrangement has been accepted.|/terms

F091|Start with the care information supplied for the actual piece and its confirmed material and finish. Use the materials and care page for general context, then ask the atelier about anything unclear. A similar-looking product or editorial image does not establish interchangeable care instructions. Include the piece or inquiry reference in the question.|/materials-care

F092|Yes. Include the confirmed material and finish where known, the piece reference and the actual use or concern. If those details are unknown, say so rather than identifying them from appearance. Photographs can explain context but cannot certify composition. Ask for guidance tied to the actual piece before choosing a cleaning or treatment method.|/materials-care

F093|No. A photograph, visualization or prop does not establish heat resistance or a temperature limit. Describe the intended use and ask for guidance based on the actual confirmed material and finish. Do not test heat exposure because a reference scene contains a candle, cup or other warm-looking object. Appearance is not performance evidence.|/materials-care

F094|No. A product name, plate-like shape or photograph containing food does not establish food-contact suitability for a proposed piece. Ask about the actual material, finish and intended use before making that assumption. A decorative illustration communicates appearance; it cannot replace the appropriate specification or supporting information for a suitability claim.|/materials-care

F095|Ask the atelier with the piece reference, confirmed specification and the specific cleaning question. Include relevant photographs if they help explain a concern. Do not choose chemicals, abrasives or repair methods from an inspiration image or a general article. Follow the instructions for the actual piece and request clarification when their scope is unclear.|/materials-care

F096|Describe nearby windows, heat sources, moisture, frequent contact and normal use where relevant. Note any recent move or change in conditions. Keep observations separate from a diagnosis of what caused a concern. These details support a piece-specific discussion; they do not establish technical exposure values or prove that the material is suitable for the location.|/materials-care

F097|Take a whole-piece view and a closer view of the area in useful light, without filters where possible. Record when it was noticed and relevant changes in use or placement. Describe what is visible rather than assigning a cause. Include the inquiry reference and consult the current concern-reporting policy before attempting repairs.|/returns-cancellations

F098|No. General guidance provides context but does not replace instructions for the actual confirmed material, finish and use. Keep piece-specific notes with the current specification and ask about any apparent conflict. Do not strengthen a broad suggestion into a warranty, certification or performance limit, or borrow instructions from an unrelated similar-looking object.|/materials-care

F099|Discuss the proposed move before assuming the original handling or installation arrangement applies. Describe the current and new positions, route, turns, stairs or lifts, and the piece's confirmed dimensions. Ask what assessment is needed. This is not a moving instruction, and the website does not promise installation at every destination.|/shipping-delivery

F100|Contact the atelier with the piece reference, the instruction you are trying to understand and the action you are considering. Include the confirmed material and finish if available. Asking a specific question is safer than guessing from a general article or photograph. Keep any clarification with the care record for that piece.|/contact

F101|State whether the image is a close-up, a whole-object view, a concept scene or a verified installation photograph. Explain what the detail is being used to show and link it to the wider source where available. Do not add a client, location or completion claim merely because the image looks realistic or has a suggestive filename.|/portfolio

F102|Design visualizations carry a disclosure indicating that they are illustrative. Concept Portfolio entries also state that they are not completed customer projects. Read that label alongside the image and caption. Realistic rendering does not establish a real installation, verified material property or exact finished appearance, and a reference image is not necessarily a rendering of the described concept.|/portfolio

F103|A genuine project needs a distinct source identity, factual brief and response, project-specific evidence, permitted attribution and publication approval. Several images of one project remain one record. The labelled concept studies are educational proposals and do not count as completed commissions. Missing evidence cannot be replaced by an invented customer, location or completion date.|/portfolio

F104|No. A room image may be a visualization, a reference or an unrelated photograph. A real installation claim needs source evidence tied to the actual project and permission for the proposed public use. Photorealism and filenames are not enough. When the source is a concept, the caption and surrounding story must keep that classification clear.|/portfolio

F105|Public attribution depends on the permission granted for that story and its images. A customer may permit an object to be shown while keeping their name, location or personal history private. The public wording should follow the actual allowed scope. Omitted details should remain omitted rather than being replaced with invented identifying information.|/privacy

F106|Genuine feedback publication requires a recorded source, permission for the intended use and approved public attribution. Do not invent an anonymous identity or assume private feedback can be published. The exact permission may allow a limited attribution, but it must be recorded. Fictional samples are separately labelled and are not customer feedback or evidence of consent.|/testimonials

F107|No. A translated quote remains the same underlying feedback record. Multiple languages, placements or images do not create additional testimonials. Preserve the original meaning and permitted attribution, and keep language review separate from source and consent approval. A machine-assisted translation is not evidence that a native reader has reviewed the published wording.|/testimonials

F108|Yes. Several views can explain one project or concept, such as an overview and a detail. They should remain tied to the same source identity where appropriate. More photographs do not mean more completed projects. Label reference images that merely inform a concept so they are not mistaken for documentation of its construction or installation.|/portfolio

F109|Use related links on the entry or browse the relevant Portfolio or Journal topic. Check the classification and purpose of each linked record: a concept study, guidance article and genuine project story answer different questions. A related link does not prove the records describe the same customer or commission. Keep useful references for the discussion.|/portfolio

F110|Identify the page and image, then ask the atelier what source or classification applies. Include the visible title or reference so the question is precise. Do not infer a customer, location, material identity or available product from the image alone. Captions and disclosures should state known information; unresolved provenance remains a question.|/contact

F111|List the decision, why it matters, the relevant proposal version and who may provide the missing information. Separate unanswered questions from preferences and confirmed agreements. Put questions that affect other choices first. A tidy list does not create agreement; keep each item pending until an actual answer or approval supports a change of status.|/commission

F112|Label the feature optional and identify the current proposal. Explain what would change and what should remain the same, then ask whether separate pricing and feasibility review are appropriate. Do not assume the option is available or included. Any revised quotation and specification need their own clear version and agreement.|/commission

F113|State the preferred period, the occasion it relates to and the amount of flexibility, if any. Ask for an individual timing discussion rather than describing the range as booked. Production and delivery estimates depend on the actual request and are confirmed separately. A saved inquiry, reference number or preferred date does not reserve a production slot.|/shipping-delivery

F114|Give each version a distinct label and date, identify which is currently agreed and mark the other as a proposed change. Describe the exact difference rather than sending two unexplained images. Keep the response with the decision log. A new attachment does not automatically supersede an approved specification or confirm that the requested change is feasible.|/commission

F115|Yes, as a clearly labelled proposal for discussion. Identify the current specification and explain the requested change without editing the old record as though approval already exists. Ask about feasibility, cost, timing and the next approval step where relevant. Changes after approved production starts are assessed individually under the current policy and are not guaranteed.|/returns-cancellations

F116|Read the current cancellations, returns and refunds page in full. It distinguishes requests before production or approved non-recoverable procurement from changes after approved work begins, and it preserves remedies for damaged, defective, incorrect or materially non-conforming products. Do not reduce those conditions to a blanket “no returns” statement. Ask about your actual circumstances using the inquiry reference.|/returns-cancellations

F117|Describe the destination, relevant access and preferred timing in the request, then discuss the actual arrangements with the atelier. Serviceability, transport, installation and charges are confirmed individually. Under the current policy, installation requires prior arrangement within Surat and international delivery is unavailable at launch. Read the full delivery page before relying on an arrangement.|/shipping-delivery

F118|Contact the atelier through an appropriate private channel, identify the existing inquiry and state the corrected detail or preferred channel. Explain whether the previous detail should no longer be used. Keep delivery-address or design changes separate unless they also need correction. Do not assume sending the preference means every relevant record has already been updated.|/contact

F119|Check the destination, inquiry reference, contact details, exact personalization text, dates, dimensions and completeness of the pasted summary. Review attachments and any extra text in the composer. Correct formatting without changing the intended meaning. You press Send yourself; the website cannot confirm that the prepared message was sent, received or read.|/faq

F120|End the summary with the unresolved decision, the information needed and who will provide it. Identify the current reference or proposal version and distinguish a preferred date from an agreed one. Keep the item visibly pending until there is an actual response. A closing message does not replace recorded approval or confirm production or delivery.|/commission
